  "findings": [
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F1",
      "proposition": "Prioritise £7 and £10 for real-behaviour testing. Their valid-case gross price-times-intent indices are £3.633 and £3.363, versus £2.673 at £4 and £2.576 at £13. Both mid-prices exceed both endpoints after Holm adjustment: £4−£7=−£0.959 (adjusted p=7.47e-9), £4−£10=−£0.690 (p=.00264), £7−£13=£1.056 (p=.0000970), and £10−£13=£0.787 (p=.0139). The £7−£10 difference is £0.270, with unadjusted 95% CI −£0.189 to £0.728 and adjusted p=.498.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/gross_proxy/values/valid_case",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/P3_GROSS_PROXY/values"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Evidence-supported testing priority; no established winner between £7 and £10.",
      "qualification": "Valid n at £4/£7/£10/£13 is 704/682/655/633; assigned n=750 each. Weight sums, ESS and module bases are in price_intent_audit. These are hypothetical indices, not revenue forecasts. Prioritisation is researcher judgment, not an identified market optimum; nonsignificance does not establish equivalence.",
      "topic_cluster": "price_test_priority"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F3",
      "proposition": "Cost assumptions change the numerical leader without establishing a superior mid-price. At costs of £0.50/£2/£3 per proxy-positive subscriber-month, valid-case contribution indices for £7 versus £10 are £3.373 versus £3.195, £2.595 versus £2.690, and £2.076 versus £2.354. The £7−£10 differences are £0.178 (unadjusted 95% CI −£0.254 to £0.611; Holm p=1.000), −£0.096 (−£0.449 to £0.258; p=1.000), and −£0.278 (−£0.580 to £0.023; p=.418).",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/contribution_cost_0_5/values/valid_case",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/contribution_cost_2_0/values/valid_case",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/contribution_cost_3_0/values/valid_case",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/P4_CONTRIBUTION_SCENARIOS/values"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Scenario-dependent numerical rankings; no adjusted evidence separating £7 and £10.",
      "qualification": "One joint Holm family covers 18 tests. Both mid-prices exceed £4 in all three scenarios. Neither significantly exceeds £13 at costs £2 or £3; at £0.50, £7 exceeds £13 (adjusted p=.00140), while £10 does not (p=.0623). £13 is therefore lower priority, not conclusively inferior under every scenario. Costs are hypothetical; indices are not profits. All price estimates and bases are retained in the audit claims.",
      "topic_cluster": "cost_sensitivity"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F4",
      "proposition": "Missing responses further weaken any single-price recommendation. Weighted nonvalid intent is 5.58%, 8.99%, 12.35% and 15.46% at £4/£7/£10/£13. Scoring nonvalid responses zero gives recorded-positive rates of 63.11%, 47.23%, 29.48% and 16.75%; all six contrasts remain significant after Holm adjustment. At the £2 cost assumption, the £10 valid-case numerical lead reverses to a negligible £7 lead: all-assigned contribution is £2.362 versus £2.358.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/intent_by_price/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/postprice_responded/values/by_price",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/P2_ALL_ASSIGNED_INTENT/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/contribution_cost_2_0/values/all_assigned"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Prespecified sensitivity preserves the recorded-interest gradient but exposes financial-ranking fragility.",
      "qualification": "All-assigned n=750 per price. The £7−£10 recorded-positive contrast is 17.76 percentage points (unadjusted 95% CI 12.79–22.72; Holm p=7.33e-12). At £2 cost, contribution pointwise intervals are £2.177–£2.546 at £7 and £2.092–£2.624 at £10; no additional financial test is claimed. Logical completion ranges are 63.11–68.69%, 47.23–56.22%, 29.48–41.83% and 16.75–32.22%; these are missing-data ranges, not confidence intervals or actual-demand bounds. Fixed baseline weights do not recover missing preferences.",
      "topic_cluster": "response_uncertainty"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F2",
      "proposition": "The price trade-off is substantial: positive stated intent among valid respondents falls from 66.84% at £4 to 51.90% at £7, 33.63% at £10 and 19.82% at £13; negative intent rises from 21.42% to 36.07%, 52.91% and 74.03%. All six valid-case contrasts survive Holm adjustment. Adjacent cheaper-minus-dearer differences are 14.94 percentage points (unadjusted 95% CI 9.59–20.29; adjusted p=4.41e-8), 18.27 points (12.90–23.63; p=7.34e-11), and 13.81 points (9.00–18.62; p=3.56e-8).",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/intent_by_price/values",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/intent_5/values/by_price",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/P1_VALID_INTENT/values"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Multiplicity-adjusted differences in valid-case stated intent.",
      "qualification": "Full five-category distributions and bases are retained in price_intent_audit. £4 could serve as a high-interest benchmark, although its gross index is below both mid-prices. Valid-case comparisons condition on post-assignment observation and do not establish actual demand.",
      "topic_cluster": "interest_price_tradeoff"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F5",
      "proposition": "Include the prespecified time-pressed-family audience in behavioural testing. At £7, households with children under 18 and weekday meal-pressure answers 4 or 5 report 62.74% positive intent, versus 47.10% among other classified households: +15.64 percentage points (unadjusted 95% CI 8.01–23.27; Holm p=.0000584). At £10, rates are 46.23% versus 28.26%: +17.97 points (10.36–25.58; p=.00000735).",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/audience_intent/values/groups",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/audience_intent/values/contrasts",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/time_pressed_family/values"
      ],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Prespecified, multiplicity-adjusted audience associations at both mid-prices.",
      "qualification": "Audience/other assigned eligible n at £7=299/444, weight sums=229.871/520.163, ESS=298.067/426.148; valid n=267/409, weight sums=205.295/477.540, ESS=266.167/392.231. At £10, assigned eligible n=302/440, weight sums=231.367/510.686, ESS=301.064/421.269; valid n=257/390, weight sums=197.291/452.306, ESS=256.210/373.791. Module bases and separate missing counts are in the group table. Unknown audience status is excluded. Attributes were not randomised; these comparisons establish neither attribute causality nor different price sensitivity between audiences.",
      "topic_cluster": "audience_priority"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F6",
      "proposition": "Use follow-up interviews to investigate price and adequate free alternatives. Among respondents with intent codes 1–3 who answered the reason question, monthly price is the main reason for 26.84% at £7 and 38.71% at £10; adequate free options account for 23.05% and 16.88%.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/reason_not_commit/values/by_price/7",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/reason_not_commit/values/by_price/10"
      ],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive diagnostic evidence supporting interview topics.",
      "qualification": "At £7, route-eligible n=314, weight sum=330.761, ESS=291.666; valid n=305, weight sum=320.060, ESS=283.461; DK/refusal/skipped counts=7/0/2; outside-route n=436. At £10, eligible n=421, weight sum=435.370, ESS=392.326; valid n=408, weight sum=422.288, ESS=380.314; missing counts=11/0/2; outside-route n=329. These selected, item-valid respondents differ across arms. No significance test was prespecified; results do not establish all-household barrier prevalence or explain the price contrast causally.",
      "topic_cluster": "followup_questions"
    }
  ],
  "story": {
    "beats": [
      {
        "order": 1,
        "finding_refs": ["F1"],
        "headline_intent": "Advance £7 and £10 as the main behavioural-test candidates.",
        "analytical_relationship": "Lead with the testing priority supported by adjusted gross-index comparisons, while making the unresolved comparison between the two candidates explicit."
      },
      {
        "order": 2,
        "finding_refs": ["F2"],
        "headline_intent": "Higher prices trade fewer positive stated responses for more value per hypothetical subscriber.",
        "analytical_relationship": "Explain the recommendation through the full intent distribution: £4 attracts the most stated interest but produces a lower gross index than either mid-price."
      },
      {
        "order": 3,
        "finding_refs": ["F3", "F4"],
        "headline_intent": "Costs and missing responses prevent a defensible single-price winner.",
        "analytical_relationship": "Qualify the recommendation with all three cost scenarios, multiplicity-adjusted contrasts and all-assigned sensitivity; retain uncertainty about £13 under higher costs."
      },
      {
        "order": 4,
        "finding_refs": ["F5", "F6"],
        "headline_intent": "Include time-pressed families and investigate reasons for hesitation.",
        "analytical_relationship": "Translate audience associations and routed diagnostic answers into follow-up priorities without claiming causal mechanisms or observed conversion."
      }
    ]
  },
  "method_notes": [
    "This revision selects and ranks the verified draft's six findings using only the four supplied files reproduced in the prompt. No tools, external sources or respondent-level data were used. Analysis claims retain rounded supplied-table summaries rather than new empirical analyses.",
    "The fictional randomised monadic study assigned 3,000 baseline-complete household meal planners to one price each, with 750 per arm. Only price varied. Results concern the specified synthetic household frame, not all UK households or actual customers. No purchase, use or retention outcome supports a launch-price conclusion.",
    "Baseline composition is retained in baseline_balance_audit before conditioning on post-price response. Exact item-specific eligible and valid bases and missing counts are at analysis_results.json#/tables/assignment_balance/values. Equal allocation does not establish identical composition. Weight sums are neither population counts nor effective sample sizes.",
    "Positive intent means exactly codes 4 or 5; valid intent means codes 1–5. Full distributions are retained. DK, refusal, skipped items and module exits remain distinct. Separate weighted DK/refusal/skipped shares are unavailable in the supplied tables and cannot be recovered from unweighted counts; weighted total-nonvalid and module-exit shares are reported.",
    "Inference follows the declared fixed-weight independent-row ratio variance, two-sided alpha=.05 and Holm families P1=6, P2=6, P3=6, P4=18 and P5=2. All quoted 95% intervals are unadjusted pointwise normal intervals. Significance decisions use adjusted p-values, not interval overlap; nonsignificance is not equivalence.",
    "Random assignment supports interpretation by assigned price within the synthetic design, but valid-case analyses condition on post-randomisation observation. All-assigned recorded-positive yield combines response and intent. Fixed baseline weights encode assumed target shares and provide neither nonresponse correction nor external representativeness.",
    "Gross=p*q and contribution=(p-c)*q mechanically treat each positive response as one subscriber-month without conversion calibration. Costs of £0.50, £2 and £3 are hypothetical, constant across prices and charged per proxy-positive subscriber-month. Indices exclude fixed development/content costs, acquisition, taxes/VAT, refunds, discounts, payment failures, retention and churn. They are not revenue forecasts or profits; no ROI, elasticity or interpolated optimum is estimated.",
    "Certainty and anticipated use are not behavioural corroboration: certainty can accompany negative intent, and anticipated use is routed only to intent codes 3–5. Reason-question percentages use route-eligible and item-valid bases.",
    "The exploratory older, comfortable, paid-planning niche remains suppressed at every price: valid n=20/15/20/16 at £4/£7/£10/£13, below the n=40 threshold. No niche rates or comparisons are reported; pooling cannot rescue price-specific evidence. Source: analysis_results.json#/tables/premium_niche/values."
  ]
}
